high.title: VN-Index Lost More Than 113 Points in One Week, Experts Identify Stock Groups in "Oversold Zone"
high.summary: Vietnam's stock market ended the first trading week of March with negative developments as VN-Index fell sharply to its lowest level in about three weeks. The index closed at 1,767 points on March 6, losing over 40 points from the previous session. Compared to the end of the previous week, the index has lost over 113 points, a very sharp decline in a short time, similar to the "tariff shock" in April 2025. Selling pressure increased amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, causing extreme investor concern. This is crucial for FX traders and bond investors as geopolitical tensions typically strengthen USD demand and create volatility in emerging market assets, potentially affecting VND exchange rates and Vietnamese bond yields.

high.title: USD and Oil Prices Rise Sharply Due to Middle East Conflict: How Do Exchange Rates and Inflation in Vietnam Get Affected?
high.summary: Early morning on February 28, 2026, the US coordinated with Israel to conduct airstrikes targeting Iran. Iran immediately retaliated against US and Israeli-related locations. This rapidly escalated Middle East tensions and increased global geopolitical risks. Oil prices surged due to supply disruption fears, while USD Index (DXY) gained 0.8% to 98.42 points, and gold prices also rose, reflecting clear "risk-off" sentiment in global financial markets. VCBS noted that in an environment of increased geopolitical uncertainty, global capital flows tend to reallocate toward safe-haven assets. This is highly relevant for VND traders as it creates upward pressure on USD/VND rates and potential inflationary pressures through higher energy costs.

high.title: Military Bank Just Increased Savings Interest Rates Sharply
high.summary: MB maintained interest rates for terms under 12 months but significantly increased rates for terms from 12 months and above. For deposits under 1 billion VND, 12-18 month rates increased from 5.5% to 6.1% annually (up 0.6 percentage points), while 24-60 month terms rose from 6.3% to 6.6% annually (up 0.3 percentage points). For deposits over 1 billion VND, similar increases were applied. This reflects broader pressure on deposit funding costs across the banking system, which could signal upward pressure on lending rates and potentially tighter monetary conditions. Bond investors should watch this as rising deposit rates often correlate with higher government bond yields.

high.title: Middle East Tensions Impact USD Prices How?
high.summary: In Vietnam, USD exchange rates have recently shown signs of increase. The State Bank of Vietnam currently announces the central rate at 25,057 VND/USD, up 13 VND consecutively over the past week. At commercial banks, USD is commonly quoted around 26,029-26,309 VND/USD (buy-sell). In the free market, USD trades at higher levels around 26,850-26,880 VND/USD. SBV Deputy Governor Pham Thanh Ha noted that escalating Middle East tensions have caused world oil prices to surge 8-13% in just a few days, creating additional pressure on global inflation. This is critical for FX and bond markets as it suggests continued upward pressure on VND/USD rates and potential monetary policy implications.

medium.title: BIDV Bank Interest Rates March 2025: Which Term Has the Highest Interest Rate?
medium.summary: BIDV maintains demand deposit rates at 0.1% annually. Short-term 1-2 month deposits are at 2.1% annually. 12-month terms apply 5.2% annually, while the highest rates of 5.3% annually apply to 24-month and 36-month terms. These rates remain stable, indicating BIDV's cautious approach to funding costs amid market pressures.

medium.title: Latest Vietcombank Interest Rates March 2026
medium.summary: Vietcombank continues to maintain stable deposit mobilization rates in early March 2026. The highest interest rates belong to long-term deposits from 24 months and above, reaching 5.3% annually, applying to both counter and online deposits. Demand deposits are at 0.1% annually, while 12-month terms offer 5.2% annually.

medium.title: Good News for All People Borrowing from Banks and Finance Companies
medium.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam is seeking opinions on a draft circular amending regulations on lending activities. The draft proposes increasing small loan limits from 100 million to 400 million VND, and borrowers of small loans won't need to provide feasible capital use plans. This regulatory easing could boost credit growth and economic activity.

medium.title: Credit Tightened, Real Estate Companies Push Bond Channel
medium.summary: HoREA Chairman Le Hoang Chau noted that while there are over 44,000 real estate companies nationwide, few are listed to effectively utilize the stock market for medium and long-term capital mobilization. In the context of tight credit control, bonds remain an important medium and long-term funding source, but companies must enhance transparency and financial capacity.

medium.title: Proposal to Reduce Import Tax on Gasoline and Oil to 0%
medium.summary: The Ministry of Finance is building a decree to amend preferential import tax rates for some gasoline, oil and raw materials. The war between US, Israel and Iran has seriously affected gasoline and oil business in Vietnam and globally. The proposal to reduce import taxes to 0% aims to help businesses be more proactive in import sources and stabilize domestic fuel supply.

medium.title: Private Bank with Largest System Just Increased Savings Interest Rate to 7% Range
medium.summary: VPBank adjusted deposit mobilization rates from March 10, 2026, with the highest rate raised to 7% annually for 12-month online deposits. Short-term 1-5 month rates remained at the maximum allowed 4.75% annually. The 12-month term saw increases to 6.9% at counters and 7% online, reflecting upward pressure on funding costs across the system.
